content.name: Iván Manfredi
content.posting_note:
Run one post a day, Monday through Friday: Eleven Booked Calls, Change One Thing, Why The Email List Stays Theirs, The Forty Percent Client Cliff, Is That A Real Case Study. Before you post any of them, read it aloud and change any line that is not how you would say it.

The two graphics are built in your own site colours and type, so use them where they fit. Every post reads fine as plain text too, so skip the graphic on any day you would rather not use one.

posts.title: Eleven Booked Calls, Zero Founder Hours
posts.body:
The accepts were fine. The replies were the part I sat with.

1,008 invites out from his own seat, every one a DTC founder scored against his ICP.

294 accepted.

New ICP connections in his own network, all of them.

119 wrote back. Warm and cold lanes.

11 booked calls, each one traced back to the message that started it. Seat opened July 13. First call August 6, eleven by September 2.

His hours on any of it: 0.

He never opened the tool.
posts.quote: Booked calls , each traced to the message that started it

image.copy: 11 booked calls, each one traced back to the message that started it

posts.title: Change One Thing At The Broken Stage
posts.body:
Read the funnel before you touch anything.

The drop tells you which stage broke. Change ONE thing at that stage, leave the rest alone.

Because if you rewrite the opener, retarget the list and move the pitch in the same week, next month moves and you can't tell which change did it.

Say accepts look fine and nobody replies. That's the first message, so that's the only thing you touch.

Replies but no calls? Open the threads and read when the pitch showed up.

One change, one stage, one month. Then read it again.
posts.quote: Find the stage that dropped, change ONE thing there, leave the rest alone.

posts.title: Why The Email List Stays Theirs
posts.body:
I'd argue with any setup where the list sits on the agency's side.

The audience, the domain and the email list belong to the client from day one, and they stay his through the contract and past any handover call.

Mattan's lead magnets sit on resources.risedtc.com. His logo, his colours, his name. Every email they capture lands on his list.

Kyle's followers are his, for good.

28,845

That number doesn't move if he stops paying me tomorrow.

And that's the test. If you fired me on Friday, what would you still have on Monday? The answer has to be everything: the audience, the email list, the content, and every lead captured.

An agency holding your list is holding a hostage. You keep paying because leaving costs you the asset.

I'd rather you stay because the calls keep landing.

So the work has to be the reason, every single month.

That's the deal I want anyway.
posts.quote: Everything stays yours: the audience, the email list, the content, and every lead captured.

posts.title: The Forty Percent Client Cliff
posts.body:
We do have a bit of that cliff that we're going to be hitting there at the end.

A marketing agency co-founder told me that last week about her biggest client. She can see it ending. She just can't say when.

That client is close to 40% of her revenue.

For years it was the stable part. Predictable number, the one she built the roster around. So nobody touched it.

And the retainer bought that client's money. It never bought their audience.

So the month they walk, 40% goes at once, and she's restarting from zero with no list of her own to email.

Her only plan right now is hoping they stay.

Hoping they stay is a countdown.
posts.quote: we do have a bit of that cliff that we're going to be hitting there at the end.

posts.title: Is That A Real Case Study
posts.body:
A marketing guru asked me whether one of the posts on the screen was a real case study.

He had one of my client feeds I run open in front of him.

Yeah. Those are real lines from his sales calls.

I never had to source ideas for that post. The founder said it out loud to one of his own customers on a recorded call. The recorder caught it, and it went out a few days later after polishing.

So when a post reads like it came from inside the business, usually it did.

That's the part you can't fake from a blank composer. You can invent a hook. You can't invent the sentence a buyer already reacted to.

Your own client calls and sales calls are the most genuine source you have.

The material is already in the recording.
posts.quote: A marketing guru asked me that, with one of my client feeds I run open on his screen.
